# SFCmodeler

## Usage

### Installation

``` sh
$ pip install SFCmodeler
```

(Doesn’t work yet :)

Install latest from the GitHub
[repository](https://github.com/slevey087/SFCmodeler):

``` sh
$ pip install git+https://github.com/slevey087/SFCmodeler.git
```

Then import with

``` py
from SFCmodeler import *
```

### Documentation

Documentation can be found hosted on this GitHub
[repository](https://github.com/slevey087/SFCmodeler)’s
[pages](https://slevey087.github.io/SFCmodeler/). Additionally you can
find package manager specific guidelines on
[pypi](https://pypi.org/project/SFCmodeler/).

## How to use

First declare
[`Parameter`](https://slevey087.github.io/SFCmodeler/term.html#parameter)s
(fixed exogenous values),
[`Variable`](https://slevey087.github.io/SFCmodeler/term.html#variable)s
(found endogenously by the solver), and any
[`Random`](https://slevey087.github.io/SFCmodeler/term.html#random)
elements, each with a `name` and optional `description` and
`initial_value`

``` python
Variable.default_value = 10  # This sets a default initial value for Variables

C = Variable("C","Consumption")
T = Variable("T","Taxes")
V = Variable("V","Wealth",100)   # The number 100 overrides the default value declared above
Y = Variable("Y","GDP")

alpha1 = Parameter("alpha_1","MPC out of income",0.6)
alpha2 = Parameter("alpha_2","MPC out of wealth",0.4)
G = Parameter("G","Government spending",5)
theta = Parameter("theta","Tax rate",0.2)
```

Next define the
[`SFCmodel`](https://slevey087.github.io/SFCmodeler/modeler.html#sfcmodel)
with a list of equations. Each equation should have one variable on the
LHS, then `<<` as the equals sign, then any valid `Sympy` expression:

``` python
model = SFCmodel(
    [
        C << alpha1 * (Y - T) + alpha2 * V(-1),
        Y << C + G,
        T << theta * Y,
        V << V(-1) + Y - T - C
    ]
)
```

Run `.solve()` to solve one period forward, or specify a number of
periods to solve more than one time step:

``` python
model.solve(5)
```

Easily shock a model by changing a parameter value with this shortcut:

``` python
model[alpha1] = 0.7

model.solve(5)
```

`.data` holds a
[`ModelResults`](https://slevey087.github.io/SFCmodeler/modelresults.html#modelresults)
object, which is a fancy pandas `DataFrame` such that you can use your
parameters and variables as indexers, or also calculated expressions,
and also quickly plot:

``` python
model.data[[Y, C(-1), alpha1*Y]]
```
